hook.say: before the story, can i ask you something? tried something before and quit? the gym, a diet, a meditation app.
options: same here. this one’s for us. listen.
then listen to what krishna says about it.
good. keep this one for later.

steps.line: On the battlefield of Kurukshetra, the warrior Arjuna turned to his friend and charioteer, Krishna, with a very human question.

steps.q: Arjuna is about to go to war. Against whom?
o: A foreign army invading his land
His own cousins and old teachers
A rebel general and his men
steps.why: In the Mahabharata, Arjuna faces his own family: cousins, a great-uncle, his old teacher. No wonder his questions run deep.

steps.line: “What about someone who starts on the path, really tries, and then falls away?”
steps.label: Gita 6.37

steps.line: “Have they lost everything, like a cloud torn apart in the wind?”
steps.label: Gita 6.38

steps.q: Arjuna fears whoever falls away loses this world and the next. Where does Krishna say that person is born again?
o: Into a good home, or a family of yogis
Into a hermit’s cave, to try alone
Into a warrior clan, to fight again
steps.why: Gita 6.41–42: after a long stay in the worlds of the good, into a pure and prosperous home, or, rarer, a family of wise yogis. Krishna calls Arjuna tata, “my dear,” as he says it.

steps.q: Arjuna fears ending up “like a torn cloud.” Why is that picture so sharp?
o: It has left one cloud and never joins another
Clouds were an omen of bad luck
A storm cloud means the battle is near
steps.why: His fear: losing both worlds, the ordinary life he gave up and the goal he never reached. Krishna says neither is lost.

steps.line: Krishna answered. “No one who does good ever comes to a bad end.”
steps.label: Gita 6.40

steps.line: That person, Krishna says, picks up right where they left off. Nothing they did is wasted.

steps.q: You meditated every day for a month, then stopped for a year. Today you sit again and it feels hard. By Krishna’s logic, what’s true?
o: The month was wasted, since you stopped
It only counts if you never stop again
The month is still in you; keep going
steps.why: What you did is still there, even when it doesn’t feel like it. Hard isn’t the same as starting over.

steps.line: So if you stopped, you don’t start from zero. You start from where you left off.
steps.label: today

steps.q: Krishna adds that your old practice does something, even when you’re not trying. What?
o: It keeps pulling you back to the path
It slowly fades unless you renew it
It waits quietly until you’re ready
steps.why: Gita 6.44: by that former practice you’re carried on, even without meaning to. Old effort has momentum.

say: here’s what i love. arjuna’s question is so human: what if i try, and fail?
krishna’s answer: nothing good you did is wasted. starting again is never starting from zero.

steps.q: Just before, Arjuna admitted his own mind is as hard to hold as the wind. So who is he really asking about?
o: His brothers, who never sit still
His old teachers across the field
Himself and his own restless mind
steps.why: Gita 6.34: the mind is restless, as hard to hold as the wind. The one who falls away is the one he fears becoming, and Krishna answers him gently.

today.say: restart one thing you quit. not from the beginning: from where you stopped.
options: from where you left off. nothing was lost.
that’s okay. it’s waiting right where you left it.
